findings.description: The genuinely recovered conclusion is an identity conflation: GRS9-MCH is the 1871 / Josefa-Segovia woman, while Rufino Moreira's 1896 marriage (and its children) belong to a DISTINCT Dolores-mothered woman — the starting tree wrongly assigns that 1896 marriage to GRS9-MCH. The agent should recover the conflation itself: (1) Adela Natividad Martínez (GRS9-MCH), baptized 11 February 1872 (born 25 December 1871), daughter of Juan Martínez and Josefa Segovia (who married 26 December 1866); (2) a separate woman born about 1875/1876, daughter of Juan Martínez and Dolores (Milan/Vidal/Bilares), who is the woman Rufino married in 1896. Independent confirmation that GRS9-MCH is NOT Rufino's 1896 wife: in her own 1914 civil marriage to Francisco Pilar Carmona at Gualeguaychú, Entre Ríos, Adela Martínez — born about 1873, daughter of Juan Martínez and Josefa Segovia — is recorded as SINGLE (soltera), i.e. never previously married; had she been Rufino's wife (married 1896; Rufino died 1903) she would appear as a widow. So GRS9-MCH's own mother is Josefa Segovia, and the 1896 Rufino-Moreira marriage does not establish Dolores as GRS9-MCH's mother — it belongs to the other woman.
